items.title: New AI tool exposes plant pathogens and the genes behind them
items.excerpt: Leiden University's bacLIFE uses machine learning across 16,000+ plant-associated bacterial genomes to flag lifestyle and disease-linked genes; knocking out six candidate genes made bacteria far worse at infecting plants (PhD thesis, Guerrero Egido). Detection/knockout only, no enhancement.

history_match.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool

items.title: AI improves cosmic particle scans to locate hidden objects more accurately in simulations
items.excerpt: University of Tartu and GScan trained ML models on both straight-through and scattered cosmic-ray muons for muon tomography; in simulations a hybrid method located hidden objects better and cut wrongly merged nearby objects from about 15% to 2% (IEEE Access).

items.title: Using AI to accelerate neuroscience research
items.excerpt: Society for Neuroscience preview of Neuroscience 2026 talks: Tsinghua's Guanglong Sun finds a shared memory-formation learning principle between artificial neural networks and fruit flies; UC Irvine's Vivek Swarup presents a plain-English AI tool for genomic data analysis. Roundup, few numbers.

items.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
items.excerpt: UC Santa Barbara and partners used a deep learning system to design electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes in a blind volunteer's visual cortex, improving control and prediction of perceived phosphene shapes (Neuron proof-of-concept).

items.title: This AI finds patterns in visual brain activity and turns them into pictures
items.excerpt: A new AI model, Brain-IT, reconstructs images from fMRI brain scans and runs the reverse, predicting what an image would look like as visual-cortex activity. (Brain decoding; cognition lane is LOW today.)

history_match.title: Scientists built an AI called 'Concept2Brain' that simulates human brain waves from pictures and text

items.title: An animal researcher explains how she decoded birdsong with AI
items.excerpt: Interview with UC Berkeley computational neuroethologist Julie Elie on combining machine learning with behavioural experiments to decode zebra finch calls and what they reveal about avian social intelligence (bioacoustics; Q&A format, not a new paper).

items.title: New AI Models Are Turbo-Charging Protein Design
items.source: GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News
items.excerpt: GEN feature: computer-designed protein therapeutics move from proof-of-concept to wet-lab validation and clinical trials; e.g. Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 designed multiple binders to the hard target TNFalpha. Industry survey feature rather than single paper.

history_match.title: AI designs working molecular scissors that recognize and cut selected protein targets

items.title: Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity's /teamwork
items.excerpt: Google's multi-agent /teamwork pairs researchers with parallel Gemini agents plus automated verifiers; results include a full Lean 4-formalized proof of the 2013 Courtade-Kumar information-theory conjecture and a machine-checked Weil conjectures formalization. (Lean/formal-proof lane is deprioritized today.)

items.title: AI Agents Ran a Biology Lab. Humans Popped in to Empty the Trash.
items.excerpt: Shanghai Jiao Tong University's AutoDNA: an AI coordinator and agents plan workflows from literature, write control code and drive robot arms across 20+ lab instruments to run DNA-storage experiments end to end, with humans only restocking (Nature). Off-list outlet: no allowed-domain coverage found.

history_match.title: AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more

items.title: Dark matter-hunting satellite Euclid reveals record number of cosmic 'magnifying glasses'
items.excerpt: Euclid's first major data release yields about 15,000 new candidate strong gravitational lenses, more than all previous catalogs combined; a four-stage pipeline starts with machine learning to parse the survey for likely lenses before citizen-science and expert review (UBC; 26 papers submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics).

items.title: Finding romance with AI: Study explores benefits, limits of chatbot intimacy
items.excerpt: University of Michigan survey of 463 U.S. adults in chatbot, long-distance and in-person relationships finds similar emotional and intellectual intimacy ratings, but in chatbot relationships emotional intimacy tracked with more loneliness unless social support was accounted for (Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans).

items.title: AI system can reconstruct aerodynamic shapes and predict their performance
items.excerpt: Kyushu University's PI-GAE, a physics-informed graph autoencoder, compresses wing and compressor-blade shapes into a few variables, rebuilds them and predicts aerodynamic performance without a full CFD run per design (Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering).

items.title: AI toolbox accelerates bioreactor simulations by up to 10,000 times
items.excerpt: TU Graz's CLARA toolbox uses unsupervised clustering to collapse millions of CFD data points into a small network of compartments, automating reduced-order bioreactor models that run up to 10,000x faster (Chemical Engineering Science).

items.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
items.excerpt: A digital twin of JWST, built by combining a physical instrument model with machine-learning optimization tools, removes starlight glare far more precisely, making faint exoplanets 2 to 15 times easier to detect and revealing a previously hidden planet in archival data.

history_match.title: Exoplanets Can't Hide From The JWST's 'Digital Twin'
